original_test_intent: Exercise one approved Redfish test event that is defined by the BIOS message registry, then prove the resulting event resolves to the intended registry and registry version; the title requires registry-version coverage that the Master Procedure and generic Criteria do not explicitly retrieve.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/BIOS firmware, EventService action schema and BIOS message registry collection/resource; export/baseline existing event logs and registry metadata; define one harmless vendor-approved event payload with a unique marker and expected MessageId/arguments/severity; require explicit approval; POST exactly once through protected TLS; capture complete response/task and correlate the new log entry by marker/time/ID; resolve its MessageId prefix/version to the authoritative registry document and compare the registry version; retain or remove only the test entry through an approved granular method, never clear unrelated history.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies and approves the harmless test-event payload, registry/version oracle and retention/cleanup policy; an agent may submit one event and collect/correlate evidence after approval.
required_inputs: BMC/BIOS firmware and supported EventService SubmitTestEvent action schema
Exact nonempty test-event payload, unique marker, expected MessageId/arguments/severity and alert/notification impact
Canonical BIOS message-registry collection/document URI, registry prefix/language/version and expected version/build compatibility
Event-log baseline/export, capacity, retention or granular cleanup, protected TLS/authentication and explicit one-shot authorization
safety_requirements: Export/preserve existing event history and verify capacity before mutation
Validate the exact target and harmless payload; never send the source's empty body by assumption
Account for notifications/alerts and use a unique correlation marker
Submit once, collect complete event/registry evidence and do not retry on ambiguity
Do not clear the entire log; stop on wrong target, unsupported action, unexpected severity/alert or missing correlation

After approval, submit exactly one event and correlate the resulting record to its registry entry/version
Apply only approved granular retention/cleanup and verify unrelated records remain
Do not invent payload/version, expose secrets, spam events, clear logs, retry or decide verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The SubmitTestEvent endpoint matches the literal Procedure, but `-d ''` supplies no defined event and the Procedure never names a registry read; DeepSeek's readback is necessary but currently invented.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After schema approval, POST one nonempty vendor payload with a unique marker, then GET the exact resulting event and canonical registry document/version through TLS-validated secret-safe Redfish; do not clear the full log.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Literal SubmitTestEvent POST, empty payload preserved as unsafe source detail, BIOS message registry version title, readable/correct criterion and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat payload, event record, MessageId resolution and registry version as a trace chain, with an immutable pre/post log diff and a one-event/no-clear policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds title coverage, nonempty schema-valid payload, unique event correlation, authoritative registry document/version, alert impact and controlled retention.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful POST only proves action acceptance; it does not prove which registry decoded the event or that the BIOS message registry version is correct. An empty body may merely return an error.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Test events can trigger external alerts and consume finite log capacity; registry documents may be localized/versioned separately from BIOS build, so MessageId prefix/version matching must be explicit.

project_override_considerations: If registry version can be verified read-only without generating an event, engineering may make submission a separate checkpoint, but must preserve the Master POST coverage as pending/waived rather than silently removing it. If individual test entries cannot be deleted, retention with a documented marker is safer than clearing the log.

Secret-redacted POST status/headers/body/task and exact correlated event record
MessageId-to-registry prefix/language/version resolution and expected-version comparison
Notification/alert observations plus retention/granular cleanup and unrelated-log integrity

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title requires a BIOS message registry version, while the Procedure only posts an unspecified empty test-event body and the Criteria merely says data is readable/correct. No registry resource, version value or readback is stated, so the title cannot be validated from the literal steps alone.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The apparent event-to-registry objective is identifiable and vendor schema/resource/version data can complete it. Those are supplyable prerequisites, so the case remains conditionally executable rather than intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2252 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00034-V001: decide whether authoritative coverage is SubmitTestEvent, BIOS message-registry version readback, or both; approve BMC/BIOS firmware, supported action schema and exact nonempty harmless payload/marker/expected MessageId/arguments/severity/alerts; canonical registry URI, prefix/language/version and expected value; baseline/export/capacity, one-shot authorization, retention or granular cleanup and no-whole-log-clear policy.

review_improvement: Preserves the state-changing EventService step while restoring the missing registry-version title coverage and preventing an empty arbitrary POST or destructive log cleanup.
independent_technical_reasoning: Redfish message registries decode MessageIds; their version is a property of the registry document, not inherently returned by SubmitTestEvent. A test event can demonstrate that one MessageId resolves under a registry, but only if the payload and resulting record are known and then linked to the exact registry prefix/version. The Master omits that chain, creating a source conflict rather than a safe executable recipe. Once engineering supplies it, the operation can be bounded to one event with preserved history and no automatic retry.
